methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $130M total raised proxy.

data.narrative:
Osmo, a Series B consumer tech company founded by Alex Wiltschko, has raised $130M to date. The valuation analysis is constrained by the absence of comparable public or private peers in the available dataset, limiting triangulation to a single methodology.

The stage-progression method applies a 1.9x multiplier to the $130M total raised as a proxy for current valuation, yielding an implied value of $247M. This multiplier reflects typical step-up dynamics between Series B and later-stage funding rounds in consumer tech. The methodology assumes that capital deployed serves as a reasonable floor and that the multiplier captures investor conviction at subsequent rounds.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $210M (low) to $284M (high), with a median of $247M. The range reflects typical variance around stage-progression estimates but remains narrow given reliance on a single method. Key uncertainties include the absence of peer benchmarking—no public or private comparables were available to validate the 1.9x multiplier against actual sector precedent—and the lack of underlying operational metrics (revenue, user growth, burn rate) that would typically anchor consumer tech valuations. A more robust analysis would require either comparable company data or detailed financial performance inputs to stress-test the implied valuation range.
